Chapter 9: The Weight of Expectations
From the very beginning, we’re taught what’s expected of us. Parents, teachers, bosses, even friends—they all have their own ideas about how life should go. What success looks like, how we’re supposed to act, what we should want. Sometimes, those expectations feel comforting, right? They give us a sense of direction and a feeling of belonging.
But on the flip side, they can also feel heavy—like a weight that presses down whenever you dare to step outside the lines.
Picture this: A young professional sitting at a family dinner, fielding questions about promotions, relationships, plans for the future. Every question is well-intentioned, but deep down, it feels like a test. Are they living up to what everyone expects? Are their choices “right?”
The pressure starts to build, and after a while, it’s tough to know where your own dreams end—and other people’s hopes begin.
Throughout this chapter, we dig into how expectations shape us, sometimes in ways we notice, and sometimes in ways we don’t. There’s the story of a high school athlete who decides to quit the team—not because they stopped loving the sport, but because all the pressure to win took the joy out of playing. Or the artist who keeps their work hidden, worried it won’t live up to what others expect.
Most of us don’t even realize how much our lives are shaped by what others think. We make choices to please, to fit in, to avoid letting people down. But here’s something to pay attention to—the people who pause and really question those expectations, who ask themselves, “What do I actually want?”—they often end up on a path that’s completely their own.
Now, let’s be honest—this isn’t easy. It means risking the possibility of disapproval, facing some uncertainty, and maybe even disappointing folks you care about. But it also means you get to live more honestly, and start discovering what really matters to you.
So, here’s the key takeaway: Expectations are powerful, no doubt about it. But they don’t have to be a prison. Most people never challenge them, but those who do? They find a freedom that’s both exhilarating—and yes, sometimes a little bit terrifying.
